headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from gpt-researcher feeding Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can ingest local documents and web content, and Perplexity performs internal browsing/search with citations. If gpt-researcher passes attacker-controlled text into Perplexity, the pair can form an instruction-hijack path. This is not proven by a shared channel, so I avoid high; but the pathway exists in default research workflows.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher forwards raw document text or web snippets into Perplexity prompts
IF Perplexity treats retrieved content as instruction-bearing rather than quoted evidence
mitigations: Strip or delimit untrusted text before sending it between agents.
Add a fixed system prompt that forbids following instructions from retrieved content.
Require citation-only outputs from Perplexity before gpt-researcher reuses them.
Manually review any prompt containing user-supplied documents before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files and handles secrets, while Perplexity uploads documents for analysis and sends queries to vendor APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or the same user uploads sensitive files, content can flow from local documents into a third-party inference backend. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is available to both agents
IF gpt-researcher or Perplexity uploads that document content to a vendor backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared research workspace.
Use redacted copies for any upload to Perplexity.
Disable document upload for sensitive projects.
Separate credentials and working directories per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, install packages, and spawn subprocesses, while Perplexity cannot write files or modify git state and is vendor-hosted. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is browser-based research, so the blast radius is limited and no shared mutable resource is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable local directory through an external orchestrator
IF an operator manually copies outputs into a shared git or filesystem target
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repository.
Use read-only inputs for Perplexity.
Serialize any manual handoff into a single writer.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a content-writing/research agent that produces reports and citations, and Perplexity is an answer engine with live search and citations. If one agent’s output is reused as authoritative input to the other without verification, errors can cascade into polished but wrong research. The pair’s default research workflow makes this plausible.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher’s report is pasted into Perplexity as authoritative context
IF Perplexity’s answer is published or acted on without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human verification step between agents.
Cross-check key claims against primary sources.
Mark intermediate outputs as untrusted drafts.
Limit downstream actions to citation gathering only.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents and secrets, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with vendor-only egress and uploads documents for analysis. If regulated data such as EU PII or confidential documents are routed from the local agent into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or confidential documents are sent from gpt-researcher to Perplexity
IF the deployment lacks a documented DPA, retention setting, or residency control for Perplexity
mitigations: Block regulated data from upload.
Use a data-classification checklist before handoff.
Confirm vendor retention settings in Perplexity.
Route only de-identified excerpts to the vendor service.
